summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the directly exposed public-company universe around education regulatory and finance rails. The strongest direct exposure is Nelnet because its public filings explicitly tie loan servicing, servicing technology, outsourcing, and education customers to Federal Direct Loan, FFELP, private education loan, and Title IV regulatory regimes. Sallie Mae is an obvious reference lender tied to private education loans but is less of a hidden compliance-rail supplier. Grand Canyon Education and Covista are direct regulated education operators/service platforms where approvals, licensure requirements, accredited institutions, and enrollment monetization make compliance rails a gating factor rather than a pure software product exposure. Expanded the universe around regulatory and student-finance infrastructure rather than obvious education operators. The strongest US-listed candidates are loan-servicing/BPO providers and buried servicing-platform vendors. Nelnet and Maximus appear most directly tied to federal student-loan servicing rails; SLM is a reference private-education-loan originator/servicer; Fiserv is a less obvious infrastructure supplier because Maximus disclosed that transferred Department of Education-owned loan accounts would continue on a Fiserv-owned servicing platform. This pass remains evidence-light on Title IV school-compliance software because many pure-play vendors appear private, acquired, or immaterial inside larger software companies.
